text:
anya: Heads up — hit a weird token-id drift after an HF->Redwood import of a quantized model (llama-3-small q4_0). Generated chat started inserting <|pad|> tokens mid-response which collapsed the stream. :eyes:

sam: Ugh. Only on quantized builds or normal too?

anya: Only saw it after the quantization step + importer run. Quick repro:
```bash
redwood import --source hf --model openlm/llama3-small --quantize q4_0 --out /redwood/models/llama3-small
```
Then run a simple chat with the canary prompt and you'll see unexpected PAD tokens consumed as if they were UNK.

anya: snippets — the HF package had an added_tokens.json with explicit ids: 
```json
{
  "added_tokens": [
    {"id": 50256, "content": "<|sep_special|>"},
    {"id": 1, "content": "<|pad|>"}
  ]
}
```
but after import the runtime vocab ends up with pad at id 0 (reserved), and something in the quantize+pack step reindexed added_tokens to fit into a dense table. logs: 
```
INFO: import: base_vocab_size=50257
WARN: added_tokens id collision -> remapping added_tokens to avoid >vocab_size
generated tokens: [50256, 0, 345, ...]  # 0 == PAD now used mid-stream
```

leo: Does the HF tokenizer define bos/eos/pad explicitly in its tokenizer.json?

anya: Yes — tokenizer.json had bos/eos/pad keys, but the importer seems to prefer the first free slot when packing into the quantized matrix, not the explicit ids. Example: 
```json
{"bos_token":"<|bos|>", "eos_token":"<|eos|>", "pad_token":"<|pad|>", "vocab_size":50257}
```
But the quantize packer assumes contiguous 0..N-1 mapping and silently reassigns to optimize layout.

mike: Not great. We previously hit something similar where added_tokens with high ids (>vocab_size) were remapped down during packing. The packer code reassigns to unused slots, and if pad/token specials are moved to index 0 it's catastrophic for streaming.

mike: Short mitigation: when importing, preserve special-token ids (fail if collision) or keep a remap-table and write it to model metadata so runtime can translate token ids.

anya: For immediate canary: remap pad back at runtime with token overrides in the serve config: 
```json
{"token_overrides": {"<|pad|>": 1}}
```
That forces the runtime to treat id 1 as pad again. Ugly but works until importer fix.

leo: Is it reproducible on non-quantized (fp16) import?

anya: I tried fp16 import and no drift — only the q4_0 path triggers the remap. So it's the quantize+pack step.

sam: Can you file a minimal reproducer and open an importer issue? We should also add a unit test in the quantize packer to check "special token identity preserved".

mike: I'll open a PR for the importer that: 1) detects added_tokens id collisions w/ vocab_size and warns+fails; 2) exposes a `--preserve-token-ids` flag that refuses to repack if true; 3) writes a remap.json alongside the model when it does remap.

anya: Thanks. I pushed a quick reproducer gist with example HF bundle and the failing chat log. Also requested a canary rollback for the affected dedicated node group (we saw customer traffic hit that cluster).

redwood-import-bot: import finished: success=1 warnings=1 remap_detected=true details=/redwood/ops/imports/1745643210/logs.txt

sam: Good. For the rollout: add an automated eval to catch BOS/EOS/PAD appearing in the middle of decode (fail if pad token id appears after decode start) so our CI can catch regressions early.

leo: Also add a small check in onboarding: if added_tokens.json contains explicit ids, ensure importer respects them or errors out. That'll prevent hidden assumptions in HF packages.

anya: Filed ISSUE-ML-512 and attached logs and a short test harness. For now we reverted the quantized model and keep fp16 in prod. :thumbsup:

mike: Will send PR link soon. If anyone needs the quick runtime override snippet lmk. :shipit:

anya: Thanks all — keeping this thread pinned until PR lands. :face_with_monocle:
